Grab ES File Explorer (Play store on Nexus Player or from PC browser).

On ES File Explorers Network tab, and turn on the FTP option - this only works while this specific tab is open, so turn it on and let it be for the moment.

You can also just use the play store in your PC browser to install compatible apps, but this limits you to the apps that Google has decided are compatible - there are apps that will work fine that will not install from the play store - and you're not getting ROMS from the play store, so there's that. I think your video is a pretty good example for me of what I don't like about it. Fisheye lens, trip hop and geek hop sound track, same old kickflips, ollies, stairs, etc. None of those things are individually bad, but when every video and magazine and movie looks like the last one, you realize that it's not going anywhere or pushing any boundaries. Sure you can do bigger tricks over bigger obstacles, but I mean the fisheye lens is probably the oldest trope in skateboarding and yet it's still a thing.

I used to skate as a kid, but for me it lost all meaning when I realized that skateboarding existed more to sell clothes to young guys than it did as any kind of legitimate sport. The official competitions like the x-games were just a joke. It was just figure skating on a wheeled plank. Listening to the commentators use the childish sounding trick names while trying to sound professional made me cringe. You can just tell that it's a sport that's always been dominated by white North American highschoolers.

It's also plagued by a toxic and immature community. I've met a handful of open minded, intellectual, and friendly people who skate, but they've been vastly outnumbered by the hordes of judgemental, small minded douchebags. Many of them have pretty poor sidewalk manners. But I think the worst thing about them is their complete lack of purpose in life. They're only interested in being "cool", it's all they live for, the approval of their peers. Then there's all the elitist sneering at other extreme sports, such as BMXing, rollerblading, and so on.

When it stops being about bratty kids whose parents have more money than sense, when it stops being about vanity, when it stops being about "cool", when it stops being a creative cesspool where ideas and originality go to die, then I might take it a bit more seriously.

I know enough about skateboarding to know that the 80's was a whole different ball game to the 90's. I arrived on the scene well after the good times had come and gone, but I was mentally conscious enough as a teen to want to know about where the pastime originated from.

I remember reading really amazing stories about early skateboarders who just went around abandoned swimming pools in California. Their abstract way of looking at the built environment, mixed with this emerging and exciting scene, must've seemed so fresh and intriguing back then. I remember being struck by how different their attitude was. They weren't interested in out-skilling everyone with obnoxiously technical tricks. Instead they were focused on having a good time.

It was this constant one-upmanship that left a bitter taste in my mouth. It wasn't about enjoying the feeling of swishing around on a halfpipe. There were no cheap pleasures here. It was about how expensive my board was, my shoes, my jeans, my shirt, and how hard the tricks I was pulling off were. It was about being better than everyone else and having more money and privilege.

I grew up in one of the biggest surfing hotspots in the world. I was all too aware that surfers invented skateboarding, and that sidewalk surfing had abandoned the skateboard in favor of the longboard a long time ago. I looked at the longboard with it's super smooth roller bearings, and luxurious bendy deck, and saw riders carving up hills like they were waves, with no care in the world. The carefree introspective zenlike attitude of the surfer is something that has stayed with them, but their skateboarding brothers have long since abandoned it in favor of more petty things.

The longboarders reminded me of the gnarly dudes who were sneaking into empty back yard pools in California. Not the manchildren you find today in skateparks. Longboarders reclaimed the skateboard and made it what it should've been; fun.
